title: Marilyn Monroe's birth chart
metaDescription: Marilyn Monroe's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 10.5° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a trine: Mars and Saturn within 0.6°, drive wired to structure. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 10.5° Gemini: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Venus. An air sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Gemini (7.0°), Venus in Aries (28.9°), Mars in Pisces (20.8°): a mind at home in argument and pattern, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mars trine Saturn, 0.6° of separation. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Saturn square Neptune at 0.8°, and Venus sextile Jupiter at 2.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Neptune while both square Saturn. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. Uranus stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mercury in Gemini at 7.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Aries at 28.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 4, water 4, fire 2 across the elements, and mutable 4, fixed 4, cardinal 2 across the modalities. An air-weighted chart thinks in through-lines; the sentence is how it takes hold of the world. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aquarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.2° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 20.6°.
